paths.description: Homepage/news front page: primary discovery surface, first-load interruption, preferences, responsive layout, performance, security and privacy.
Algemeen section listing: representative category/listing template.
Lead football story: representative article/detail template and homepage-to-article core flow.
Search results for klimaat: representative findability/results template. Search form interaction itself was not exposed on the direct result route.

findings.summary: Dark preference is ignored
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture; the preference probe reports color-scheme normal and body background rgb(255,255,255).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces/text with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Notification solicitation obscures core news on every fresh load
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, homepage, and article screenshots show a centered notification modal covering the lead story before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not open the notification solicitation on initial load; offer it after a relevant user action and preserve dismissal.

findings.summary: Modal uses an invalid ad-hoc role instead of dialog
findings.evidence: The overlay probe finds a DIV role=button with aria-modal=true; there is no dialog element and no role=dialog.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog with showModal(), labelled heading, focus containment, Escape, and an explicit close button.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport layout rather than container responsiveness
findings.evidence: The preference/CSS probe found no @container rules, despite cards and navigation being reused across wide and narrow columns.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container-type to reusable card/nav regions and use @container for local layout changes, with existing viewport rules as fallback.

findings.summary: Several controls and images lack accessible names
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found four unnamed controls, including search/settings and carousel arrows; the image audit found three missing alt values in its loaded sample.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon button a stable accessible name and provide meaningful alt text or alt="" for decorative images.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly exposed on primary controls
findings.evidence: The active-focus probe found no outline or box-shadow on most sampled links/buttons, including logo, top navigation, menu, and article links; several top-nav targets are only 14-16px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and ensure compact controls have at least a 24px minimum target, preferably 44px for touch.

findings.summary: 404 state is a dead end
findings.evidence: The exercised unknown URL says the page could not load but exposes no retry, home, search, or relevant-content links in main.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a real 404 response with Home, search, and current-news recovery actions; avoid the internal “Error detected” copy.

findings.summary: Initial rendering is slow and main-thread work is heavy
findings.evidence: Trace recorded FCP 2.78s, LCP 5.58s, four long tasks, longest 452ms, and 808ms total blocking time. Lighthouse on the mandatory privacy-gate journey corroborated 3.9s LCP.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP asset, remove redirect/gate latency where possible, and defer/chunk advertising, experimentation, and analytics work.

findings.summary: Network delivery is dominated by scripts and third parties
findings.evidence: HAR captured 191 requests and 2.57MB transferred, including 1.57MB script and 1.80MB from third-party origins; two classic head scripts are parser-blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical classic scripts, conditionally load ad/experiment stacks, trim dependency chains, and set durable cache headers.

findings.summary: Images do not reserve intrinsic space
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports all 100 inspected images lack width and height attributes; Lighthouse also flags unsized images, even though the short layout observation saw CLS 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every image so space is reserved before image decoding.

findings.summary: Large script payload includes avoidable unused and duplicate work
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 61 scripts and 1.57MB script transfer; Lighthouse estimates 58KiB unused JavaScript, while advertising and experimentation bundles are among the largest resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to remove unused modules, deduplicate tag-manager loads, and load third-party features only when their UI is reached.

findings.summary: Browser hygiene is weakened by inspector and BFCache issues
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports a cookie issue and three BFCache blockers on the privacy-gate journey; a third-party source map also returns 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve cookie inspector issues, avoid unnecessary no-store responses on navigable pages, and ship valid source maps for maintained scripts.

findings.summary: Core content is absent from raw HTML and AI crawlers are explicitly blocked
findings.evidence: Discoverability reports 0% homepage and 1% article raw-content coverage, no raw title/h1/description, and isJsShell=true. robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, OAI-SearchBot and other AI agents.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render article/listing content and metadata. If broad AI exclusion is intentional, document it; otherwise allow desired agents while retaining explicit content-use policy.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP posture is too permissive
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; 22 of 26 observed first-party-domain cookies lack Secure and many use SameSite=None. HTTPS, HSTS, and nosniff are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Harden CSP with nonces/hashes and strict-dynamic where appropriate; mark every HTTPS cookie Secure and use Lax/Strict unless cross-site delivery is required.

findings.summary: Tracking footprint is disproportionate
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 52 third-party origins and nine known tracker domains; HAR attributes 157 requests and 1.80MB to third parties, while fresh-load cookies include long-lived advertising/experiment identifiers.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, delay non-essential tracking until valid consent, shorten identifier lifetimes, and batch essential analytics.

findings.summary: Defensive header policy is incomplete
findings.evidence: CSP has no frame-ancestors directive, X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy are absent, and Permissions-Policy grants only a client-hint rule rather than explicitly restricting sensitive features.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors, strict-origin-when-cross-origin (or stricter) Referrer-Policy, and an allowlist-based Permissions-Policy; remove unsafe CSP sources.

findings.summary: News content depends on JavaScript
findings.evidence: Raw fetches contain only 22 text characters and no title, h1, or description while rendered pages contain thousands of characters; both tested templates are classified as JS shells.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve headline, article/listing content, and navigation in the initial HTML, then hydrate enhancements.

findings.summary: Failure recovery lacks useful actions
findings.evidence: The tested 404 route shows only an error message and no links or retry/search action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide purposeful network/404 states with retry, search, home navigation, and preserved context.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bandwidth
findings.evidence: All 100 inspected images use legacy JPEG URLs, 24 lack srcset, 25 are over twice displayed width, and 10 below-fold images are not lazy loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP variants through picture/srcset, size candidates to display density, and lazy-load non-critical images.

findings.summary: Third-party budget outweighs first-party delivery
findings.evidence: HAR records 1.80MB third-party transfer versus 0.77MB first-party, with 157 of 191 requests third-party; tag management, ads, and experimentation are leading costs.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party request/byte budget, remove low-value vendors, and load remaining integrations after interaction or consent.

findings.summary: Repeated menu use retains substantial additional heap
findings.evidence: After ten menu open/close cycles, same-session JS heap rose from 47.6MB to 58.4MB while DOM nodes stayed at 2,857; independent post heap was 53.2MB versus 48.1MB baseline. This is medium-confidence retained-growth evidence, not a proven leak trace.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the repeated interaction with forced-GC baseline/target/final snapshots and remove retained listeners, arrays, ad objects, or timers identified by retaining paths.

findings.summary: Baseline heap is heavy for a news listing
findings.evidence: The baseline heap contains 906,269 nodes, 4.52M edges, 48.1MB self-size, 83,032 closures, and 221,969 objects before extended interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial vendor execution and object churn; lazy-initialise advertising, experiments, and widgets only when needed.

findings.summary: Large reserved advertising area delays the news visually
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots devote roughly the first 150px below navigation to empty reserved space before the lead story, while the notification overlay further obscures content.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse or cap empty ad slots and avoid reserving a large first-viewport gap when no ad is rendered.

findings.summary: Heading and focus structure is inconsistent across templates
findings.evidence: The category and search templates expose no h1; the focus probe shows most controls without a visible focus style. Lighthouse also found invalid heading order on the consent journey.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every template one descriptive h1, keep heading levels sequential, and implement a consistent :focus-visible treatment.

taskList.title: Server-render public news content and metadata
Remove or defer the load-time notification interruption
Cut third-party scripts, trackers, and transfer cost
Harden cookies, CSP, and browser policies
Fix keyboard focus, control names, heading structure, and targets
Modernise responsive image delivery and reserve image space
Add useful recovery actions to 404/network failures
Investigate and bound retained heap growth
Adopt container queries for reusable cards/navigation
